title: Learn the numbers product managers use
summary: PMs use a small set of numbers to see whether a product works: how many people try it, how many stay and whether a change made a difference. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you do need to read numbers well.

beginner: Learn four ideas: a funnel (how many people complete each step), retention (how many come back), a north star metric (the one number that shows value) and an experiment (comparing two versions). Write one example of each from a product you know.
Read the funnel analysis guide. Sketch a funnel for signing up to a service you use, mark where you think people drop off and say why.
Read how a retention analysis is built. Describe how you would check whether people were still using a new feature a month later.
Read about north star metrics. Write one for a product you know, then list two other measures that would warn you if chasing it caused harm.
Read an introduction to controlled experiments. Note what makes a result trustworthy: a clear hypothesis, enough users, a long enough run and one change at a time.
If you want to go further, spend an hour on the interactive SQL lessons in the sources. Understanding how to ask a database a question helps with every conversation with analysts.
Take one chart or statistic from a news story and list the questions you would ask before trusting it.

toolExamples.google-docs: Keep a one-page glossary of the terms with an example for each.
toolExamples.claude: Ask it to explain one measure with a made-up example, then check the explanation against a source.

definitionOfDone: One example of each of the four ideas
A sketched funnel with guessed drop-offs
A list of questions for one chart
pitfalls: Chasing a single number without checking side effects
Reading small changes in small samples as proof
Skipping the basics to jump straight to dashboards

sources.title: Trustworthy online controlled experiments (Kohavi, Tang and Xu, Cambridge University Press)
